questions.question: Which of the following national leaders of India inaugurated the first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samman Samaroh held in Ujjain in 1958?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra Prasad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, inaugurated the **first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samman Samaroh** in Ujjain in 1958.
 
• The event was organized to honor the legacy of **Kālidāsa**, one of the greatest Sanskrit poets and playwrights in Indian history.
 
• It was held in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, a city historically linked to Kālidāsa and considered a significant cultural and literary hub.
 
• The initiative aimed to celebrate Indian classical literature, art, and culture, and promote Sanskrit poetry and drama in modern times.
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad, a renowned scholar himself, was deeply involved in promoting Indian heritage and culture during his presidency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kālidāsa:**

 
 
• Often referred to as the **Shakespeare of India**, Kālidāsa is celebrated for works like *Shakuntala*, *Meghadūta*, and *Raghuvaṃśa*.
 
• His literary works are deeply rooted in Indian culture, mythology, and philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Ujjain:**
 
 
• Ujjain, an ancient city in Madhya Pradesh, is historically associated with Sanskrit literature and figures like Kālidāsa.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage and as a center for learning and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samaroh:**
 
 
• The event is an annual celebration of classical literature, art, and culture in honor of Kālidāsa.
 
• It includes performances, scholarly discussions, and exhibitions showcasing Indian heritage.
 
 
 
• **Role of Rajendra Prasad:**
 
 
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad was deeply committed to preserving and promoting India’s cultural and literary traditions.
 
• As the first President of India, he played a pivotal role in fostering national identity through art and culture.

questions.question: In rat-hole mining, which of the following minerals is mined?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rat-hole mining** is a primitive and hazardous method primarily used to extract **coal**, especially in regions like Meghalaya, India.
 
• The process involves digging small, narrow tunnels, often just big enough for a single person to enter and extract coal manually.
 
• This method is prevalent in the unregulated and informal mining sector, particularly in northeastern India.
 
• Coal extracted through rat-hole mining is used for local consumption and sometimes sold in nearby markets.
 
• Despite its economic benefits for local communities, the practice is associated with severe environmental, health, and safety risks, including landslides and water contamination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Environmental Impact:** Rat-hole mining causes severe environmental degradation, including deforestation, water contamination from acid mine drainage, and soil erosion.
 
• **Health Hazards:** Workers involved in rat-hole mining often face significant health risks, including respiratory issues due to coal dust and a lack of proper safety measures.
 
• **Legal Status:** Rat-hole mining is banned in India under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, but it continues illegally in some regions due to weak enforcement and local economic dependency.
 
• **Economic Dependency:** Many local communities in northeastern India, especially in Meghalaya, rely on rat-hole mining as a primary source of income, despite its illegality and associated risks.
 
• **Alternatives to Rat-hole Mining:** Sustainable mining practices and proper legal enforcement can reduce dependency on such environmentally and socially harmful methods.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct temples of Khajuraho?

a) Equal importance is given to human experience and spiritual pursuit.

b) Jain and Hindu temples are also found at Khajuraho.

c) Chausanth Yogini temple is one of the important temples here.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Khajuraho temples reflect a unique fusion of **spirituality and human experience**, with intricate carvings that depict various aspects of life, including divine and human pursuits.
 
• These temples are not limited to a single religion; both **Hindu and Jain temples** coexist at Khajuraho, showcasing religious harmony during that era.
 
• The **Chausanth Yogini Temple**, dedicated to 64 Yoginis, is a prominent and historically significant structure in Khajuraho.
 
• The temples of Khajuraho are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, renowned for their architectural brilliance and detailed erotic sculptures.
 
• These temples were built by the **Chandela dynasty** between 950 and 1050 AD, highlighting the advanced architectural skills of medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khajuraho Temples:**

 
 
• There are **22 surviving temples** out of the original 85, grouped into three categories: Western, Eastern, and Southern groups.
 
• The temples are known for their **Nagara-style architecture**, characterized by curvilinear spires and intricately carved exteriors.
 
• The sculptures depict four major themes: **spiritual teachings, love, royalty, and everyday life**.
 
 
 
• **Chausanth Yogini Temple:**
 
 
• This is one of the **oldest temples** in Khajuraho, made of coarse granite.
 
• It is an open-air temple dedicated to **64 Yoginis**, representing tantric traditions.
 
 
 
• **Chandela Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Chandela rulers were great patrons of art and architecture and were responsible for the construction of the Khajuraho temples.
 
• The temples were strategically located in a remote area to avoid destruction during invasions.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1986**.
 
• It was recognized for its **mastery of art** and demonstration of the cultural heritage of India.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in the month of Chaitra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramnavami**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ramnavami** is a Hindu festival celebrated to mark the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu.
 
• It falls on the **ninth day (Navami)** of the Shukla Paksha (waxing phase of the moon) in the month of Chaitra, as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• The festival is observed with great devotion and enthusiasm across India, especially in Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Rama.
 
• Devotees chant hymns, recite the **Ramayana**, and conduct rituals like **Ram Katha recitation** and **Rama Navami puja**.
 
• It usually falls between March and April in the Gregorian calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chaitra Month:**

 
 
• The month of Chaitra is the first month of the Hindu lunar calendar and is considered highly auspicious.
 
• It marks the beginning of the spring season and is associated with new beginnings and renewal.
 
 
 
• **Lord Rama:**
 
 
• Lord Rama is considered the epitome of dharma (righteousness) and is highly revered in Hinduism.
 
• He is the central figure of the Hindu epic **Ramayana**, which narrates his life and deeds.
 
 
 
• **Ayodhya:**
 
 
• Ayodhya, located in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, is regarded as the birthplace of Lord Rama.
 
• Special celebrations, processions, and rituals are organized in Ayodhya during Ramnavami.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Navami:**
 
 
• Navami refers to the ninth day of the lunar fortnight and is considered highly auspicious in Hindu traditions.
 
• Many Hindu deities' festivals, including Ramnavami, are celebrated on this day.

questions.question: Gluten formation is observed in various foods like pasta, noodles, pizzas, and bread. Gluten occurs when two specific proteins are mixed with water. Name the two proteins responsible for gluten formation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glutenin and Gliadin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gluten is formed by the interaction of two specific proteins: **Glutenin** and **Gliadin**, found in wheat and related grains.
 
• When mixed with water, **Glutenin** and **Gliadin** combine to create a cohesive and elastic network known as gluten.
 
• Gluten provides the **elasticity and structure** to dough, allowing it to stretch and trap gases during fermentation, which is essential for bread making.
 
• Foods like pasta, bread, pizza, and noodles rely on gluten formation for their chewy texture and structural integrity.
 
• The strength of the gluten network depends on the type of flour and the protein content in it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glutenin:**

 
 
• A high-molecular-weight protein that provides **strength and elasticity** to the gluten network.
 
• Its long chains contribute to the dough's ability to stretch without breaking.
 
 
 
• **Gliadin:**
 
 
• A low-molecular-weight protein that adds **extensibility and viscosity** to the dough.
 
• It helps the dough flow and allows it to expand during fermentation.
 
 
 
• **Gluten-Free Diet:**
 
 
• People with gluten intolerance or celiac disease must avoid gluten-containing foods such as wheat, barley, and rye.
 
• Alternatives include gluten-free grains like rice, quinoa, and corn.
 
 
 
• **Celiac Disease:**
 
 
• An autoimmune disorder where the ingestion of gluten leads to damage in the small intestine.
 
• Symptoms include abdominal pain, bloating, diarrhea, and malnutrition.
 
 
 
• **Role of Water in Gluten Formation:**
 
 
• Water activates the proteins Glutenin and Gliadin, allowing them to bond and form the gluten network.
 
• The amount of water added affects the dough’s texture and consistency.

questions.question: The village servants or functionaries, who constituted of groups of families in Vijayanagar empire, were called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ayagars**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **ayagars** was used to refer to village servants or functionaries in the Vijayanagar Empire who performed essential administrative, economic, and social duties.
 
• Ayagars consisted of **12 hereditary roles**, including village accountants, priests, blacksmiths, barbers, and other service providers, ensuring the functioning of village administration.
 
• They were often paid through a share of the village produce or land grants known as **inam lands**.
 
• The ayagar system contributed to the decentralized governance model of the Vijayanagar Empire, ensuring efficient management at the village level.
 
• This system was crucial for maintaining agricultural productivity and social harmony in villages during the Vijayanagar period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayanagar Empire:**

 
 
• The Vijayanagar Empire was established in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka Raya and lasted until 1646.
 
• It was known for its contributions to art, architecture, literature, and efficient administration.
 
• The empire's capital was Hampi, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Decentralized Administration:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagar Empire employed a decentralized administrative structure, where local governance was carried out through village communities and ayagars.
 
• This system helped in effective management and ensured the welfare of the rural population.
 
 
 
• **Inam Lands:**
 
 
• Inam lands were tax-free lands granted to ayagars in exchange for their services to the community.
 
• These grants were hereditary and formed the basis of the ayagar system's sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Social Hierarchy:**
 
 
• The ayagars were integral to the hierarchical social structure, maintaining order and supporting agricultural and economic activities.
 
• They ensured the smooth functioning of villages and were accountable to the local rulers or administrators.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the West Central Railway Zone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jabalpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The headquarters of the **West Central Railway Zone** is located in **Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The West Central Railway (WCR) was **established in 2003** as one of the 18 railway zones in India.
 
• This zone primarily serves the states of **Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The zone operates a network of significant routes, including the **Kota-Bina, Jabalpur-Bhopal, and Itarsi-Nagpur** sections.
 
• The Jabalpur division is known for its strategic importance in freight and passenger operations, contributing significantly to the Indian Railways network.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Railway Zones:**

 
 
• Indian Railways is divided into **18 zones**, each managed by a Zonal Railway headquarters.
 
• The zones are further divided into divisions, each headed by a Divisional Railway Manager (DRM).
 
 
 
• **West Central Railway (WCR) Highlights:**
 
 
• WCR operates in the central region of India and plays a pivotal role in connecting major cities and towns.
 
• It is known for its focus on both passenger and freight traffic.
 
 
 
• **Jabalpur:**
 
 
• Jabalpur is a significant city in Madhya Pradesh and serves as a major hub for Indian Railways operations.
 
• The city is also known for its historical and cultural significance.
 
 
 
• **Additional Railway Zones:**
 
 
• Other railway zones include Northern Railway (New Delhi), Southern Railway (Chennai), and Eastern Railway (Kolkata).
 
• Each zone has its distinct jurisdiction and operational priorities.

questions.question: On 11th December 2022, who among the following took over as the Deputy Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mukesh Agnihotri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mukesh Agnihotri** was sworn in as the **first-ever Deputy Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh** on 11th December 2022.
 
• He is a senior leader of the **Indian National Congress** and has represented the Haroli constituency in the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly since 2003.
 
• Agnihotri served as the **Leader of Opposition** in the Himachal Pradesh Assembly from 2017 to 2022.
 
• He assumed the position of Deputy CM under the leadership of Chief Minister **Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu**, after the Congress party's victory in the 2022 Himachal Pradesh Assembly elections.
 
• The Congress party formed the government by securing a majority of **40 out of 68 seats** in the state assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himachal Pradesh Assembly Elections 2022:**

 
 
• The elections were held on **12th November 2022**, and the results were declared on **8th December 2022**.
 
• The Congress party ousted the BJP government, continuing the state's tradition of alternating power between the two parties every five years.
 
 
 
• **Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu:**
 
 
• He was sworn in as the **15th Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh** on 11th December 2022.
 
• He is known for his grassroots leadership and has been active in Himachal Pradesh politics for decades.
 
 
 
• **Deputy Chief Minister:**
 
 
• This position is not constitutionally mandatory but is often created to give representation to senior leaders or different regions within a state.
 
• Mukesh Agnihotri's appointment as Deputy CM was part of the Congress's strategy to ensure balanced leadership in the state.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges for the New Government:**
 
 
• The Congress government faces challenges such as addressing unemployment, improving infrastructure, and managing the state's financial health.
 
• Himachal Pradesh's economy relies heavily on agriculture, horticulture, hydropower, and tourism, requiring focused development policies in these sectors.

questions.question: The famous folk dance 'Dholacha Nachi' is performed in which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Dholacha Nachi'** is a famous folk dance performed in the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• This dance form is often showcased during festivals, weddings, and cultural events within the rural communities of Maharashtra.
 
• Performed predominantly by men, this dance involves rhythmic movements accompanied by the beats of the **dhol** (a traditional drum).
 
• The dance reflects the vibrant culture, traditions, and energy of the people of Maharashtra.
 
• It is particularly popular among the tribal communities of the state, symbolizing joy and celebration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Folk Dances in Maharashtra**:

 
 
• Other notable folk dances of Maharashtra include **Lavani**, **Koli**, and **Tamasha**.
 
• Lavani is known for its powerful rhythm and is often performed by women, while Koli represents the fishing communities of the state.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Dhol**:
 
 
• The **dhol** is a traditional percussion instrument widely used in Indian folk music and dances, particularly in Maharashtra.
 
• It produces a deep, resonant sound that energizes the performers and audience alike.
 
 
 
• **Regional Art and Culture**:
 
 
• Maharashtra has a rich cultural heritage that includes folk music, theatre (like **Tamasha**), and various traditional crafts.
 
• These art forms play an integral role in preserving the identity and traditions of the region.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Influence on Folk Dance**:
 
 
• Folk dances like 'Dholacha Nachi' are deeply influenced by the customs and rituals of tribal communities in Maharashtra.
 
• They often depict stories, nature, and communal bonding through expressive movements and music.

questions.question: The position of the President in the Indian Political system is that of a _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nominal Executive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India is the **constitutional head of the state** and occupies a position of a Nominal Executive.
 
• As per the Indian Constitution, the President **acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers** headed by the Prime Minister (Article 74).
 
• The President's role is primarily ceremonial, with the **real executive power vested in the Prime Minister** and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The President is bound to act as per the advice of the Cabinet in most matters, except in specific discretionary situations, such as appointing a Prime Minister in case of a hung parliament.
 
• This system ensures that India functions as a **parliamentary democracy**, where the President symbolizes unity while the Prime Minister leads the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nominal Executive:**

 
 
• A Nominal Executive is a ceremonial head of state without real political power, such as the President in a parliamentary system.
 
• The real power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers in such systems.
 
 
 
• **Real Executive:**
 
 
• The Real Executive is the authority responsible for decision-making and governance.
 
• In India, the Real Executive is the Prime Minister along with the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Discretionary Powers of the President:**
 
 
• The President can exercise discretionary powers in certain situations, such as appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority.
 
• Other instances include returning a bill for reconsideration or dissolving the Lok Sabha if advised by the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary System:**
 
 
• In a parliamentary system, the executive is accountable to the legislature.
 
• India adopted this system from the British model, ensuring a balance between the ceremonial and functional roles in governance.

questions.question:
Which of the following is an example of a physical change? In this example, there is no change in chemical composition of matter.

A: Coal changing into coal ash on burning

B: Preparing a sweet drink by mixing sugar in water

C: White washing walls using a solution of lime and water

D: Mixing salt and lemon juice in a beaker
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 - Only B: Preparing a sweet drink by mixing sugar in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Physical Change:** A physical change is a type of change in which the form of matter is altered, but its chemical composition remains unchanged.
 
• **Dissolving sugar in water** is a physical change because the sugar molecules disperse in the water without forming a new substance.
 
• The process is reversible; the sugar can be retrieved by evaporating the water, leaving the chemical composition of the sugar intact.
 
• In this example, no chemical bonds are broken or formed, and the sugar retains its chemical identity.
 
• Other examples of physical changes include melting, freezing, condensation, and breaking a material into smaller pieces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Change:** A chemical change involves a transformation where the chemical composition of a substance changes, resulting in the formation of new substances.
 
• **Example of Chemical Change:** Burning coal to form coal ash is a chemical change because the carbon in coal reacts with oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and ash, substances with different chemical compositions.
 
• **Reversibility:** Physical changes are generally reversible, while chemical changes are often irreversible under normal conditions.
 
• **Indicators of Chemical Changes:** Common indicators include the emission of gas, change in temperature, formation of a precipitate, or a change in color.
 
• **Whitewashing:** In whitewashing (lime and water), slaked lime reacts chemically with carbon dioxide in the air to form calcium carbonate, a chemical change.

questions.question: Which state lies in the rain shadow region of the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu lies in the rain shadow region** of the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon due to the obstruction caused by the Western Ghats.
 
• The Western Ghats block the monsoon winds, forcing them to shed most of their moisture on the windward side, leaving Tamil Nadu on the leeward side with reduced rainfall.
 
• This phenomenon results in Tamil Nadu receiving **less rainfall during the southwest monsoon** and making it dependent on the northeast monsoon for the majority of its annual rainfall.
 
• Tamil Nadu receives about **35% of its rainfall during the southwest monsoon**, which is significantly lower compared to other states on the windward side of the Western Ghats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rain Shadow Effect:**

 
 
• A rain shadow is a dry region on the leeward side of a mountain range due to the obstruction of moist air by the mountains.
 
• As air ascends the windward side of the mountain, it cools, condenses, and precipitates, leaving little moisture for the leeward side.
 
 
 
• **Southwest Monsoon:**
 
 
• The southwest monsoon originates over the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal and brings heavy rainfall to most parts of India from June to September.
 
• The Western Ghats force the monsoon winds to rise, causing orographic rainfall on the windward side.
 
 
 
• **Northeast Monsoon:**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu heavily relies on the northeast monsoon (October to December) for its primary rainfall.
 
• The northeast monsoon is driven by retreating monsoon winds and is a critical source of water for the state’s agriculture and drinking water supply.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• This mountain range runs parallel to the western coast of India and plays a critical role in influencing the monsoon patterns.
 
• The Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage site and are known for their rich biodiversity and ecological significance.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are an example of a non-tax revenue receipt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Non-tax revenue receipts** are those revenues earned by the government through sources other than taxes.
 
• **Interest income** is an example of non-tax revenue as it represents the earnings from loans given by the government to states, union territories, or other entities.
 
• **Disinvestment** receipts, while not a tax, are categorized as capital receipts, not non-tax revenue.
 
• Other examples of non-tax revenue include dividends from public sector enterprises, fees, penalties, and fines.
 
• Income tax (Option 3) is a direct tax, while external commercial borrowings (Option 4) are liabilities, not revenue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Tax Revenue:**

 
 
• This includes income from dividends, profits of public enterprises, fees, fines, and royalties.
 
• It is a significant source of revenue for the government apart from taxes.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment:**
 
 
• This involves the sale of government stakes in public sector undertakings (PSUs) and is categorized under capital receipts.
 
 
 
• **Income Tax:**
 
 
• It is a direct tax levied on the income of individuals or entities by the government.
 
 
 
• **External Commercial Borrowings:**
 
 
• These are loans availed by the government or private entities from foreign sources, adding to liabilities rather than revenue.

questions.question: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched by the Government of India in the year _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched by the Government of India in **2016** to promote apprenticeship training.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **financial support to establishments** undertaking apprenticeship programs.
 
• Under NAPS, the government reimburses **25% of the stipend** payable to apprentices, subject to a maximum of Rs. 1,500 per month.
 
• The scheme also provides financial assistance to establishments for **basic training costs** of apprentices who come directly without formal training.
 
• NAPS is implemented by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and is a step towards improving **employment opportunities and skill development** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Apprenticeship Training:**

 
 
• Apprenticeship training is a system of training where trainees receive **on-the-job experience and classroom instruction**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in bridging the gap between industry requirements and the skills of the workforce.
 
 
 
• **Skill India Mission:**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, it aims to train over 40 crore people in India in various skills by 2022.
 
• It includes schemes like Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), NAPS, and the creation of skill development centers.
 
 
 
• **National Policy on Skill Development and Entrepreneurship:**
 
 
• Introduced in 2015, it provides a framework for skill development initiatives across sectors and states.
 
• Emphasizes industry partnerships and private sector involvement in skill training programs.
 
 
 
• **Role of MSDE:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is responsible for implementing skill training schemes like NAPS.
 
• It ensures collaboration between government, industries, and training providers to enhance workforce employability.

questions.question: Which of the following Hindi novels is written by Vishnu Prabhakar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ardhanarishwar**__.

questions.question: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in the year _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1799**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in **1799** between the British East India Company and the Kingdom of Mysore under Tipu Sultan.
 
• The war culminated in the **siege of Srirangapatna**, where Tipu Sultan was killed in battle.
 
• The war was part of a series of Anglo-Mysore Wars fought between the British and Mysore over control of South India.
 
• The British forces were led by **General George Harris**, and they received support from the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Marathas.
 
• The war resulted in the **annexation of Mysore** by the British and the establishment of a subsidiary alliance with a puppet ruler.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tipu Sultan:**

 
 
• Tipu Sultan, also known as the **Tiger of Mysore**, was a prominent ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore.
 
• He was known for his administrative reforms and his use of advanced military techniques, including the famous **Mysorean rockets**.
 
• Tipu Sultan resisted British expansion in South India and allied with the French against them.
 
 
 
• **Anglo-Mysore Wars:**
 
 
• The Anglo-Mysore Wars were a series of four wars fought between the British East India Company and the Kingdom of Mysore (1767–1799).
 
• The wars were driven by the British desire to dominate South India and Mysore's resistance under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan.
 
 
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:**
 
 
• After Tipu Sultan's death, the British imposed a **subsidiary alliance** on Mysore, making it a princely state under British control.
 
• The alliance system was a key strategy used by the British to expand their influence in India.
 
 
 
• **Srirangapatna:**
 
 
• Srirangapatna was the capital of Mysore and the site of the decisive battle that ended the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
 
• The fall of Srirangapatna marked the end of Mysore's independence and its integration into British India.

questions.question: Literal meaning of 'megalith' is _____________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a big stone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **'megalith'** originates from the Greek words "mega" meaning **large** and "lithos" meaning **stone**.
 
• Megaliths are large stone structures or monuments, often associated with ancient cultures and practices.
 
• They were primarily used for ceremonial purposes, burial sites, or markers for significant locations.
 
• Examples of megalithic structures include **Stonehenge in England** and dolmens found across Europe and Asia.
 
• Megalithic architecture often showcases the engineering and cultural advancements of ancient civilizations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Megalithic Culture:**

 
 
• Megalithic cultures are found worldwide, including Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas.
 
• These cultures often used megaliths for funerary purposes, religious rituals, or astronomical observations.
 
 
 
• **Types of Megaliths:**
 
 
• **Dolmen:** A stone table-like structure often used as a burial site.
 
• **Menhir:** A single upright stone, sometimes arranged in rows or circles.
 
• **Cairn:** A mound of stones built as a memorial or marker.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• Megaliths provide insights into ancient civilizations' societal structures, beliefs, and engineering capabilities.
 
• They are often considered sacred and hold archaeological importance for studying human history.
 
 
 
• **Famous Megalithic Sites:**
 
 
• **Stonehenge** (England): A prehistoric monument and UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• **Göbekli Tepe** (Turkey): One of the earliest known megalithic temples.
 
• **Newgrange** (Ireland): A burial mound with astronomical alignments.

questions.question: What approach did Dadabhai Naoroji use to calculate the Poverty Line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prisoner menu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji, also known as the "Grand Old Man of India," was the first to scientifically estimate the Poverty Line in India.
 
• He used the "Prisoner menu" approach, which calculated the minimum subsistence needs based on the food provided to prisoners in colonial jails.
 
• The "Prisoner menu" included basic food items such as rice, dal, and salt, which were considered adequate for survival.
 
• Naoroji's calculations focused on the cost of food consumption necessary for basic survival, excluding other aspects like housing and clothing.
 
• This method marked the beginning of poverty measurement in India and laid the foundation for future economic studies on poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji:**

 
 
• He was an Indian nationalist, economist, and one of the founders of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Naoroji is known for his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India," where he explained the economic exploitation by the British.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament in 1892.
 
 
 
• **Drain of Wealth Theory:**
 
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji proposed the "Drain of Wealth Theory," which highlighted how British policies led to the economic exploitation of India.
 
• This theory explained how resources and wealth were transferred from India to Britain without adequate returns.
 
 
 
• **Modern Poverty Line Calculations:**
 
 
• Today, poverty lines are calculated based on multiple factors including income, consumption patterns, and access to basic services.
 
• The Tendulkar Committee (2009) refined poverty line estimation by considering broader parameters like health and education.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• During colonial India, poverty was widespread due to economic exploitation and lack of industrialization.
 
• Naoroji's work provided a framework for understanding poverty in India under British rule.

questions.question: At which of the following places was the first Singh Sabha founded in 1873?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amritsar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first Singh Sabha was founded in **Amritsar in 1873** to revitalize Sikhism and counter Christian missionary influence.
 
• It aimed to restore Sikh faith, practices, and traditions that were impacted by the British colonial regime and societal changes.
 
• The Singh Sabha focused on the **promotion of Punjabi language**, Sikh culture, and education among the Sikh community.
 
• Prominent figures in the establishment of the Singh Sabha included **Sardar Thakur Singh Sandhawalia** and other Sikh reformists.
 
• The movement later expanded to other regions, including Lahore and other parts of Punjab, laying the foundation for future Sikh reform movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Singh Sabha Movement:**

 
 
• The Singh Sabha movement was a **Sikh revivalist movement** started in the late 19th century to counter the impact of proselytization by Christian missionaries and the Arya Samaj.
 
• It focused on **educational reforms**, including the establishment of schools and colleges to promote Sikh ideals.
 
• It sought to codify Sikh scriptures and practices, emphasizing the teachings of Guru Granth Sahib as the central religious text.
 
• The movement also worked to eliminate caste discrimination and strengthen community identity among Sikhs.
 
 
 
• **Impact of British Colonialism:**
 
 
• During British rule, several religious and social reform movements emerged to address societal changes and challenges posed by Western influences.
 
• Christian missionaries actively sought converts, leading to the formation of movements like the Singh Sabha to preserve indigenous religions.
 
 
 
• **Language and Education:**
 
 
• The Singh Sabha emphasized the use of **Punjabi in Gurmukhi script**, which was a significant step in preserving Sikh culture and identity.
 
• Educational institutions established by the movement included the **Khalsa College Amritsar**, which became a center for Sikh studies and learning.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Singh Sabha movement laid the foundation for the **modern Sikh identity** and played a key role in shaping Sikh political and social organizations.
 
• Its focus on education, language, and religious reforms continues to influence Sikh institutions and thought today.

questions.question: Who was the Prime Minister when the 11th Fundamental Duty was incorporated into the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Bihari Vajpayee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to the Indian Constitution through the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
• This amendment introduced the duty to provide opportunities for education to children aged 6 to 14 years under Article 51A(k).
 
• The 86th Amendment also made elementary education a **Fundamental Right** under Article 21A.
 
• Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the Prime Minister of India when this amendment was enacted.
 
• It emphasized the responsibility of parents or guardians to ensure education for their children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties were incorporated into the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002:**
 
 
• Introduced Article 21A, which made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Amended Article 45 to make early childhood care and education a directive principle of state policy.
 
• Added Article 51A(k), making it the responsibility of parents or guardians to provide education to their children.
 
 
 
• **Atal Bihari Vajpayee:**
 
 
• Served as the Prime Minister of India three times: 1996, 1998-1999, and 1999-2004.
 
• Under his leadership, several landmark initiatives, including the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), were launched to promote universal education.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act:**
 
 
• The RTE Act, 2009, was enacted to implement Article 21A and ensure free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It mandates that private schools reserve 25% of seats for children from economically weaker sections.

questions.question: The Indian Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change maintains a log of all the endangered species of India along with their conservation status. What is the name of this book?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Data Book**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Red Data Book** is a comprehensive document maintained by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in India, listing endangered and threatened species of flora and fauna.
 
• It categorizes species based on their conservation status, such as **extinct, critically endangered, endangered, vulnerable, and least concern**.
 
• This book serves as an important resource for **tracking biodiversity loss** and helps in formulating conservation strategies.
 
• Globally, the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** maintains the Red List, which is an international version of such a document.
 
• India's Red Data Book includes species like the **Bengal Tiger, Indian Bustard, and Ganges River Dolphin**, which are critically endangered.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endangered Species:**

 
 
• An endangered species is one that is at a very high risk of extinction in the wild due to factors such as habitat loss, hunting, or climate change.
 
• In India, examples include the **Snow Leopard, Nilgiri Tahr, and Red Panda**.
 
 
 
• **IUCN Red List:**
 
 
• The IUCN Red List is a global inventory of the conservation status of plant and animal species.
 
• It uses scientific criteria to classify species into categories ranging from "Least Concern" to "Extinct."
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in India:**
 
 
• India is one of the world's 17 **megadiverse countries**, hosting about 8% of the world's biodiversity.
 
• Conservation efforts include programs like **Project Tiger, Project Elephant, and Biosphere Reserves**.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972:**
 
 
• This act provides the framework for protecting endangered species and their habitats in India.
 
• Under the act, hunting and trade of endangered species are prohibited, and wildlife sanctuaries and national parks are established.
